confirmed.description: Ibrahim's scar is mirrored onto his RIGHT cheek. He is in profile facing screen right, with his ear at screen left, so the cheek we see is his right cheek, and pale scar lines are drawn across it from the ear to the beard. The bible and the script both put the scar on his LEFT side, from ear to jaw, and every other panel in the chapter keeps it there.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of page-10.png around (215-290, 420-480) in the 1325-wide frame: several pale diagonal scar strokes run between the visible ear and the mouth on the camera-facing (right) cheek. The ash is correct.

verdict.reason: The art does show it. In 10.1 Ibrahim stands at screen left in three-quarter view facing screen right, with his ear at screen left, so the cheek we see is his RIGHT cheek. I zoomed into both the page render (page-10.png, about x 300-400, y 560-660 at 1838 px) and the source frame (frames/page-10-panel-01-v01-2x.png). On that right cheek, thin pale strokes run through the beard: one curve sweeps down from below the ear, and two or three diagonals run toward the corner of the mouth. Luminance is about 120-140 on the strokes against about 80-100 on the skin around them. They are drawn the same way as his real scar on page 8, panel 8.1, where he faces screen left: thin pale lines, one of them crossed, on the LEFT cheek. Page 6, panel 6.1, where he also faces screen right, shows a clean right cheek. So page 10 is the one panel that puts the scar on the wrong side, against the bible's and the script's LEFT ear-to-jaw scar, which the script explicitly guards against mirroring. I am rating it minor, not major. At print size his face is only about 11 mm tall and the strokes are about 3-4 mm long, hairline-thin and low in contrast. I did not notice them in the full-page view, they are only faint at 1:1, and a casual reader could take them for grey in his grey-flecked beard. It is fixable by painting out the strokes on the right cheek, with no redraw needed. The ash on his forehead is correct.

confirmed.description: Nagoji's hands change from fully linen-wrapped to bare hands with wrist cuffs inside one scene. In 1.1 and 1.3 the palms and backs of both hands are wrapped in clean linen, as the bible's chapter 5 row and the script ask. On page 2 only narrow cuffs at the wrists remain, and the palms and fingers are bare. In 2.5 the script calls for 'one bandaged hand flat against' the wall, but the hand is drawn bare.
confirmed.evidence: 2.5: the hand pressed to the wall at the top left shows bare fingers and palm, with a linen cuff at the wrist only. 2.2 and 2.3: wrist cuffs only, bare hands resting on the knees. Compare 1.1, where both hands are wrapped over the knuckles in his lap.

verdict.reason: Partly refuted, and what is left is minor. The headline claim about 2.5 is wrong. When zoomed in, the hand pressed to the wall at top left has linen wound over the palm and the back of the hand up to the knuckles and around the wrist. Only the fingers and thumb are bare, which is the same wrap seen in 1.3, where the fingers also show past the bandage. So the script beat "one bandaged hand flat against it" is drawn, and no beat is missing. The other hand in 2.5 sits on his hip, mostly hidden, with a wrist wrap. The part that holds up is in 2.2 and 2.3: Nagoji's wraps shrink to narrow cuffs at the wrists, and both hands are bare from the knuckles down, clasped on his knees. That drifts from 1.1, where both hands are bound almost to the fingertips, and from the bible's chapter 5 row ("hands wrapped in clean linen"). At print size these are small figures in half-width panels. The wrist bandages still read as wounded, bandaged wrists, and the chapter 1 to 3 bible rows describe "bandaged hands and wrists". So this is a polish-level drift of how much is wrapped, not a costume error that needs a redraw. If touched up, 2.2 and 2.3 should wrap the backs of the hands over the knuckles, as in 1.3 and 2.5.

confirmed.description: The cart and its load change between two consecutive panels, and the carter disappears. 3.4 shows a low open cart bed loaded with pale cream cloth sacks, woven palm-leaf baskets and the open pepper sack, with the carter at the yoke. 3.5 shows a taller cart with slatted rails and big brown jute bales tied with rope, no carter, and Ibrahim standing at the yoke pole. Pages 4 to 6 follow the 3.5 version, so 3.4 is the panel that breaks.
confirmed.evidence: 3.4: white sacks and wicker baskets, a low side board, and the bare-chested carter with a topknot and goad on the right. 3.5: a spoked-wheel cart with an upright slatted rack and brown burlap bales, and no carter in frame.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 3, comparing crops of 3.4 and 3.5. In 3.4 the cart is a low, open bed with a plain plank side. It carries pale cream cloth sacks and woven palm-leaf baskets, and one sack is open on black pepper. In 3.5, the panel right beside it, the cart is a tall spoked-wheel cart with upright slatted rails, stacked high with brown burlap bales tied with rope. Pages 4.1, 4.4, 5.2, 5.5, 6.1 and 6.2 all keep the 3.5 cart: brown jute sacks and slatted rails. That leaves 3.4 as the only panel that doesn't match. Because the two panels sit next to each other, the change in colour (cream against brown) and in shape (low board against a tall rack) is easy to see at print size. Script 3.4 does say "sacks of plain coarse cloth and woven palm leaf", so 3.4 follows its own description. But the script never asks the cart to change, and 4.2 to 6.2 have the men sitting "on the sacks" of the same cart. So this is a continuity break, not something the script allows. The cheapest fix is to redraw the load in 3.4 to match the rest of the chapter. One part of the report does not hold: the carter's absence in 3.5 is not an error. The 3.5 description only calls for Nagoji in the foreground and Ibrahim half turned to the bullocks. The cast file lists only ibrahim and nagoji, and the carter can simply be out of frame. Severity is major (a localized prop and continuity error, not an identity or lettering problem).

confirmed.description: Nagoji's tunic sleeves are rolled up to just below the elbows, so both forearms are bare down to the wrist cuffs. The bible's chapter 5 row and the page 3 cast block say the left sleeve stays down over the brand. In the same hall scene (7.1, 7.3, 8.1, 10.1) his sleeves reach the wrists, so the sleeves change length within the scene. The bare left forearm also shows no brand.
confirmed.evidence: 9.1: Nagoji standing at the edge of the mat. Both cuffs are bunched below the elbows, and his left forearm (screen right, beside Ibrahim) is bare skin from the elbow to the linen wrist wrap.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on a 2x crop of page 9, panel 9.1. Nagoji's cream tunic sleeves are rolled into thick cuffs at or just below the elbows. Both forearms are bare skin down to the linen wrist wraps, and this is easy to see at print size. The page 3 cast block in the script, which runs to the end of the chapter, calls for "long sleeves" and "the left sleeve down over the brand". In 7.3 the official's eyeline is aimed at that covered left sleeve on purpose. Every other shot of the hall scene shows the sleeves full length to the wrist: 7.1, 7.3, 8.1 and 10.1, and also 10.2. So the costume changes for one panel in the middle of a continuous interview, and it undoes the covered-brand beat. One part of the original report is weaker: the missing brand. His left forearm hangs with the inner side turned toward his thigh, so the brand on the inner forearm would not face the camera anyway. The bible's chapter 5 row does not mention sleeves; only the script cast block does. The real fault is the sleeve length. It is a localized costume and continuity error, not a wrong identity, so it rates major. The fix is to redraw 9.1 with the sleeves down to the wrists.

confirmed.description: Both Nair gate guards wear modern short-sleeved shirts: a turned-down collar, a button placket down the front and rolled sleeve cuffs. They read as 20th-century shirts rather than 1740s short cotton jackets (the script asks for short white cotton jackets, or bare chests). The left guard is the speaker of the panel's first balloon, so the anachronism sits in the establishing shot of the compound.
confirmed.evidence: At 4x zoom on the left guard (about x 1150-1330, y 665-860 at full resolution) the camp collar, a row of placket buttons and folded-back sleeve cuffs are clear under the crossed strap. The right guard by the open gate leaf wears the same shirt. Their spears, round shields, topknots and dark sashes are correct; only the shirts are wrong.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 6, panel 6.1. I zoomed 4x on both gate guards (left guard about x 1140-1340, y 640-900; right guard about x 1500-1680, y 650-900) and also checked them at native 300 DPI print scale. The left guard, who speaks "You come late, kapitan", wears a modern short-sleeved shirt: a pointed turned-down collar, a front button placket with visible buttons, and rolled cuffs. The right guard wears the same shirt with the same collar and cuffs (his placket is less clear). The script's cast note and beat 6.1 both call for "short white cotton jackets" or bare chests, and no line in the continuity bible allows collared shirts. At print size each guard is only about 0.6 in wide, but the collar points and rolled sleeves still show and give the figure a 20th-century look. Both guards stand prominently in the chapter's establishing shot of the compound. The hall guards in 6.3 and 6.4 wear crossbelts and open vests, so the 6.1 shirts also clash with the rest of the page. The spears, round shields, topknots, dark sashes and mundus are correct. The error is localized and limited to the costume, so it is major, not a blocker.

refuted.description: Nagoji is off-model in the reverse wide. His hair is flat, straight and slicked back into a low tail instead of long black curls. His face is longer and gaunter than on the nagoji-v2 sheet, and neither ear shows the gold stud even though both ears are visible. At this size, the moustache, tunic and bandages are the only things that say this is Nagoji. In 9.2, right below, he is fully on-model with curls and a stud, so the change is jarring.
refuted.reason:
Refuted. The reviewer's coordinates are in the downscaled display. In the full 1838x2775 page, Nagoji's head in 9.1 sits at about x 960-1100, y 520-640. A 4x zoom of that area shows the following:
(1) Hair: it is drawn swept back and tied at the nape, as the CONTINUITY.md Chapter 5 row requires ("From page 3: ... bare-headed, hair tied back"). The script's continuity note says the same ("hair tied back"). It is also not flat or straight: the zoom shows wavy locks at both temples and behind the ears. The bible asks for exactly this look, so it cannot count as off-model.
(2) Face: it is lean and long-jawed, but the nagoji-v2 sheet face (FRONT and THREE-QUARTER views) is also long, lean and high-cheekboned. The 9.1 face has his strong cheekbones, straight nose, thick curled moustache and clean chin. The difference from the 9.2 close-up comes from lens and angle, not from a different identity.
(3) Ear stud: the whole head is about 120 px tall, roughly 0.4 inch at 300 DPI print. A small stud at that scale would be 2 or 3 px, too small to read in print. Missing it is too slight to matter.
Identity is also clear in context: the balloon tails point to him, and he has the collarless cream tunic, both bandaged wrists, and Ibrahim (turban, beard, vest, ash) leaning in at his shoulder. The shift to loose curls in the 9.2 close-up is ordinary close-up treatment, not an identity error. If anything, 9.1 follows the bible's tied-back hair more closely than 8.1 does.

refuted.description: Ibrahim has no ash on his forehead. The bible's chapter 5 row puts the ash on him from 5.3 to the end of the chapter, and the page 6 cast note repeats it for every panel. It is present in 5.4, 5.5, 6.2 and 6.3 but missing here, between them.
refuted.reason: The reviewer is right on the facts but wrong about how much it matters, so I'm refuting it as too slight to matter at print size. The page is drawn at print size (1838 px wide at 300 DPI, about 6.1 in). In panel 6.1, Ibrahim's forehead is indeed bare. The bible does call for ash from 5.3 to the end of chapter 5, and the script repeats it for page 6. At 5x zoom there is no ash under the turban, while 6.2 and 6.3 show it as white lines. But 6.1 is a wide establishing shot. Ibrahim's whole head, turban to beard tip, is only about 95 px at print size (about 8 mm). He is in three-quarter view facing right, and the turban sits low, so only a strip about 10 to 12 px high (about 1 mm) shows between the turban edge and the brow. Even in the medium shots the script asks for a 'faint ash smear', and it is only about 8 px tall in 6.2. In 6.1 it would be a sub-millimetre speck. At actual size (the native-resolution crop), I can't tell whether the ash is there or not in 6.1, but the turban, beard, vest and stole all read clearly as Ibrahim. Comics routinely drop a mark this small in a long shot, and no reader would see a break between 6.1 and 6.2. It is not 'major'. If anyone wants it fixed, it is at most an optional minor retouch.

refuted.description: The reading order of the four-balloon exchange is unclear. The balloons zig-zag: question 1 is in the centre, Nagoji's 'Yes.' is at the far left, question 2 is at the right at almost the same height as 'Yes.', and 'Some.' is back in the centre at the bottom. Reading strictly top to bottom gives Q1, Q2, Yes, Some, so the answers come apart from their questions.
refuted.reason:
I cropped and zoomed panel 7.3 on page 7 at full resolution (1838 px wide). The balloon positions are about what the reviewer measured. In full-res crop coordinates the boxes are: Q1 '<You raided them?>' y 455-572; Q2 '<You know their forts?>' y 540-657, at the right; 'Yes.' y 575-683, at the far left; 'Some.' y 650-768, lower centre. The zig-zag is there, but it does not cause the misreading the reviewer describes.

(1) Q1 is clearly the first balloon: its bottom (572) is above the top of 'Yes.' (575).

(2) 'Yes.' and Q2 overlap vertically for most of their height (82 of about 117 px), so they sit on the same tier. The usual comics rule for balloons on the same tier is left before right. That puts 'Yes.' before Q2 and gives the order the script asks for: Q1, Yes, Q2, Some. The reviewer's 'strictly top to bottom' ordering, based on a 15 px (scaled) difference between balloon tops, is not how readers actually move through a panel.

(3) Even if a reader takes the stepped Q1-Q2 pair first, the exchange still makes sense. The tails are correct: both questions point to the official's head and both answers point to Nagoji. The answers come in the same order as the questions, and 'Some.' only fits 'You know their forts?'. So the reader gets 'two questions, then two answers' and pairs them correctly. The answers do not come apart from their questions in any way that changes the meaning.

At most this is optional polish. Raising 'Yes.' slightly above the top of Q2, or dropping Q2 a little lower, would fix the order beyond doubt. It is not a major lettering error and does not need to be redrawn.

minors.description: Ibrahim faces screen left toward Nagoji, so his LEFT cheek is toward camera, but neither the scar nor the forehead ash is drawn. The bible requires the ash from 5.3 to the end of the chapter. His face is also leaner and more hawk-nosed than the round, fleshy face on his sheet.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-09.png at (790-880, 400-480): clean forehead under the turban rim and no scar line on the visible left cheek.

minors.description: Ibrahim's forehead ash is missing. The script and the bible's Ibrahim chapter 5 row require it in every panel from 5.3 to the end of the chapter. It is present in 5.3-5.5 and 6.2 onward, but not here.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-06.png at (290-380, 380-450): the strip of forehead below the turban rim is bare skin with no ash mark.

minors.description: Nagoji's ear ornament is drawn as a hanging gold drop or bead earring, not the small flush gold stud the bible requires. The drop copies the nagoji-v2 sheet. 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 6.2 and 9.2 correctly show a stud, so the ornament also changes from panel to panel within the chapter. Per the 2026-10-02 author decision, the author treats this as a known deviation to list, not something to reopen automatically.
minors.evidence: Crops: page-02.png 2.4 (640-900, 1170-1380) shows a two-bead drop. page-04.png 4.4/4.5 show a ball hanging from a loop. page-07.png 7.3 shows a pearl drop. page-09.png 9.2 shows a correct flush stud.

minors.description: Ibrahim's LEFT-side scar is on the correct side but is drawn as a red or pink raised line. The script asks for a bare pale line through the beard. This copies the known fault on the Ibrahim sheet. In 8.1 the scar is also drawn as crossed hash marks rather than one line from ear to jaw.
minors.evidence: Crops: page-01.png 1.2 (750-860, 700-790) and page-02.png 2.1 (500-680, 270-400) show a reddish line from the ear down through the beard. page-08.png 8.1 (410-490, 385-460) shows an X-shaped pair of strokes.

minors.description: In Nagoji's lowered-head bow, the moustache is a smooth, featureless black blob with no hair texture or curled tips. It does not read as the thick curled moustache on his sheet and looks pasted on.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-10.png at (400-560, 340-470): the moustache is a solid black lozenge under the nose with flat edges.

minors.description: Look-alike in the same frame as Ibrahim. The net-mender who glances down the path wears a cream turban-style head wrap and a short grey-flecked beard, which are exactly Ibrahim's two identifiers. The script relies on 'turbaned and bearded' to single Ibrahim out, so two such men in one panel weakens that.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-03.png at (490-660, 410-560): a bare-chested net-mender with a wrapped cream head cloth and a grey-flecked beard, a few inches from Ibrahim, who is walking beside Nagoji.

minors.description: The carter is not consistent and does not match his script lock, which is a thin young man, clean-shaven, 'nothing like Ibrahim'. He is clean-shaven in 3.4, has a moustache in 5.2, and has a short beard in 5.5.
minors.evidence: page-05.png 5.2 crop (960-1080, 560-690): a topknotted carter with a moustache. 5.5 crop (320-560, 1620-1800): the carter at the yoke has a short beard. page-03.png 3.4: clean-shaven.

minors.description: Kanka in the memory bleed has a pale white streak on her forehead under the forelock that reads as a white star marking. The approved Kanka sheet is solid black with no white markings.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-02.png at (300-420, 1180-1270): a distinct white patch between the forelock and the eye. The Kanka sheet (19-kanka-v15.png) shows an all-black face. It may be meant as a specular highlight, but it reads as a marking.

minors.description: The carter is missing. The script has 'the carter walking at the yoke' in this wide shot, and the carter is present before (3.4) and after (5.2, 5.5, 6.1). Here no one drives the bullocks.
minors.evidence: 4.3: only Nagoji and Ibrahim, sitting on the sacks, and the white bullocks are in frame. No bare-chested young man with a topknot and goad is at the yoke or on the road.

minors.description: Ibrahim shows neither his ash nor his left-side scar. He stands in profile facing screen left, so his left cheek faces the camera, but no pale scar line runs through the beard from ear to jaw. No ash shows below the turban either. Both should carry through this panel.
minors.evidence: 9.1: the turbaned figure beside Nagoji, seen in left profile. The cheek and beard between the ear and the jaw are unmarked, and there is no white smear on his forehead.

minors.description: Seen from behind in the foreground, the official's hair reads as short grey hair with a gold pin across the crown, not the topknot the script asks for ('topknot ... dark in the near foreground'). The gold pin is new jewellery that he wears in no other panel. In 7.3, from the same rear angle, he has a large grey topknot bun.
minors.evidence: 9.1, foreground left: a grey head of short hair with a gold rod laid across the top, partly cut off by the balloon. Compare the bun topknot from behind in 7.3.

minors.description: Nagoji's dhoti now has a gold border, a kasavu-style stripe down the front fold and along the hem. The bible and the script specify a plain village cotton dhoti, and it is plain on pages 3 to 9.

minors.evidence: 2.5: heavy brown blotches and spatters across the cream dhoti at his hips and legs. 2.2 and 2.3 show the same cloth clean.

minors.description: Ibrahim's footwear changes inside the hall. He wears sandals on the mats in 9.1 but is barefoot in 10.1, which is the same moment of the same audience.
minors.evidence: 9.1: dark leather sandals on Ibrahim's feet as he stands on the mat. 10.1: Ibrahim barefoot on the polished floor.

minors.description: The hall guards wear red or maroon sashes. The gate guards in 6.1 wear dark sashes, and the page 6 cast note specifies a 'dark sash' for all guards. The guard dress drifts between panels on the same page.
minors.evidence: 6.4: both background guards wear deep red waist sashes, and the right-hand guard has an open white jacket. 6.3: the guard on the platform side has a red sash. 6.1: the gate guards' sashes are dark navy.

minors.evidence: Upper-left background of the panel, between the woman carrying a water pot and Nagoji (about x 190-280, y 530-650 at full resolution): a bare-backed man walking away in blue shorts, with a small figure in a white short-sleeved top just behind him.

minors.description: The carter is missing. The script has him walking at the yoke, but the cart drives itself: Nagoji and Ibrahim sit on the front of the sacks right behind the bullock and nobody is at the yoke. The carter is back in 5.2, 5.5 and 6.1, so this one panel breaks continuity.

minors.description: The script tags this line IBRAHIM (small), a quiet aside, but it is set as the biggest lettering element in the panel. It is a tall narrow balloon in normal-size type that covers about a third of a small panel.
minors.evidence: The 'Rest. The road is long, and the bulls do not hurry.' balloon runs one to three words per line over six lines and fills the middle of the panel, between the cart and the temple.

minors.description: The mare echo of Chapter 1, 6.5 is incomplete. The adaptation notes say it should repeat that panel exactly: the mare's neck and mane on a winter morning, with a man's cheek against her mane. Here there is only a full bridled horse head against a sunrise river with palms and a hilltop fort. The figure embracing the mare is gone, so the repeat does not land exactly on the Chapter 1 wound.
minors.evidence: In Chapter 1 page 6 bottom (ch01-v2 r14), a red-turbaned man presses his cheek to the mare's neck. In Ch5 page 2's third tier, the mare's head and bridle stand alone in the ink-splash bleed and no human figure is present.

minors.description: The silent flicker beat only half reads. The script wants Ibrahim's gaze to slide off Nagoji toward the bright doorway and the sea. Instead he looks up and screen-left into a dark interior with oil lamps, and there is no doorway or sea. Because Nagoji sits screen-left, Ibrahim reads as looking over Nagoji's head rather than away from him. The pose also nearly repeats 1.4 (three-quarter close, hand at the jaw), so the change between the two panels is weak.
minors.evidence: Crop of the page 1 bottom tier: Ibrahim's eyes are turned up-left, the background is a dim wall with a lamp at right, and there is no bright opening. His thumb is at the jaw under the scar, as in 1.4.

minors.description: The script asks for a close on Nagoji breathing in the pepper while the two men walk the paddy track. The render is a large waist-up shot with Nagoji sitting on the ground, knees up and bandaged hands on his knees. That adds a stop between 3.2 (walking) and 3.4 (arriving at the cart) that the script does not have.
minors.evidence: Page 3 middle tier (the largest panel on the page): Nagoji is seated, forearms resting on raised knees, framed from the waist up, with the pepper-vine tree at right.

minors.description: The staging is reversed. The script has Ibrahim's white turban leading in single file and Nagoji's head turned to catch a scent, which prompts 'Pepper.' Here Nagoji walks in front and Ibrahim follows, and Nagoji looks straight ahead. In 3.1 the two also walk side by side with Nagoji half a step ahead instead of Ibrahim leading him inland.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of page 3 top-right: Nagoji, small at left, walks ahead along the bund toward screen left facing forward, and Ibrahim is a pace behind him. Page 3 top-left: Nagoji is slightly in front of Ibrahim.

minors.description: Nagoji looks the wrong way. The script says he looks back at the boys running alongside and pointing at him. The boys are at screen left, but his head and eyes are turned screen-right, away from them, so the 'Who is he?' exchange loses his reaction.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of page 5, second tier: the boys point from the left edge. Nagoji, seated on the sacks at center-right, faces right toward the carter.

minors.description: The script asks for a tight shot with the stylus poised above the leaf, waiting for the name. The render is a medium shot from chest to waist with the top of the official's head cut off by the panel border, and the stylus tip is already on the leaf, as if he were writing.
minors.evidence: Page 6 bottom-right crop: the crown of his head is cropped at the top border, his torso fills most of the frame, and the stylus point rests on the palm leaf.

minors.description: The lettering placement departs from the script's direction. The two bow captions run along the floor at the bottom of the panel, by Nagoji's feet, instead of around his lowered head. The official's second balloon sits low at knee level between the two men instead of high beside him, so the 'lowered gaze' caption lands far from the lowered head.
minors.evidence: Page 10 top tier: 'Not as a subject, not yet,' and 'but as a man who understands...' are at y of about 920-1010 (display scale) along the panel's bottom edge. The '<Tomorrow we take you to the king's war hall...>' balloon is at mid-panel height, below the official's lap.

minors.description: The script marks both of Ibrahim's lines as whispers ('This is not the king...' and 'This is one of his hands on this coast.'). They are lettered in the standard solid balloons, the same as normal speech, so the delivery cue in the script is lost.
minors.evidence: Page 6 middle-right panel: both Ibrahim balloons have the same solid outline and type size as every other balloon on the page. There is no dashed or whisper treatment.
